_doc: §164m (2026-09-27): EVENT (mid-quarter, Reg 31(1)(c)) shareholding rows whose stored as-on date is wrong by months or years. The as-on date comes from NSE's corporate-share-holdings-master 'date' field; for these filings it carries the allotment date or a mistyped year, while the filing's own XBRL DateOfReport says the pattern's real date. fetch_shareholding.apply_event_redate() moves the row (load_events AND save_events, so a re-ingest cannot bring the wrong key back). If the target date already holds the SAME filing (equal values) the two merge and keep the earliest publication; a different filing at the target is left alone (re-adjudicate).

Found answering Quantmac v3 (JUSTDIAL blanked Feb-Jun 2019: the 400-day cap met an as-on 2018 row filed 2019). Scan: 62 event rows filed > 90 days after their as-on date; 36 match the XBRL DateOfReport, 16 differ — 10 by a few days (allotment vs report date, no effect on the series, left), 3 would land on a quarter-end that already has the quarterly row (ERIS 2019-12-31, MBLINFRA 2024-06-30 x2 — left, re-adjudicate), 6 moved here. Evidence: ~/stocks-cache/shp/eventdates/asons.json.
